hadith_m1_part2: The best fasting after Ramadan is the month of Allah, Muharram, and the best prayer after the obligatory prayer is the night prayer.
hadith_m1_book: Narrated by: Abu Hurairah | Authenticated by: Muslim | Source: Sahih Muslim | Page or Number: 1163
hadith_m2_part1: The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ used to learn this supplication just as they learned the Quran, to say when a new month or year began:
hadith_m2_part2: O Allah, bring it upon us with security, faith, safety, Islam, protection from Shaytan, and the pleasure of the Most Merciful.
hadith_m2_book: Narrated by: Abdullah ibn Hisham | Authenticated by: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani | Source: Al-Isabah | Page or Number: 2/378
hadith_m7_part2: Time has come back to its original state which it had when Allah created the heavens and the earth; the year consists of twelve months, of which four are sacred — three are in succession: Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar, which comes between Jumada and Sha'ban.
hadith_m7_book: Narrated by: Abu Bakra Nufai | Authenticated by: Al-Bukhari | Source: Sahih al-Bukhari | Page or Number: 3197
hadith_m8_part2: Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to fast until we thought he would never stop fasting, and he used not to fast until we thought he would never fast. I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ complete the fast of an entire month except for Ramadan, and I never saw him fast more in any month than he fasted in Sha'ban.
hadith_m8_book: Narrated by: Aisha (Mother of the Believers) | Authenticated by: Al-Bukhari | Source: Sahih al-Bukhari | Page or Number: 1969
hadith_m9_part2: Whoever stands in prayer during Ramadan out of faith and hope of reward, all his previous sins will be forgiven.
hadith_m9_book: Narrated by: Abu Hurairah | Authenticated by: Al-Bukhari | Source: Sahih al-Bukhari | Page or Number: 37
hadith_m10_part2: Whoever fasts Ramadan and then follows it with six days of Shawwal, it will be as if he fasted for a lifetime.
hadith_m10_book: Narrated by: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari | Authenticated by: Muslim | Source: Sahih Muslim | Page or Number: 1164
hadith_m11_part2: Time has come back to its original state which it had when Allah created the heavens and the earth; the year consists of twelve months, of which four are sacred — three are in succession: Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar, which comes between Jumada and Sha'ban.
hadith_m11_book: Narrated by: Abu Bakra Nufai | Authenticated by: Al-Bukhari | Source: Sahih al-Bukhari | Page or Number: 3197
hadith_m12_part2: Two months do not diminish — the months of two Eids: Ramadan and Dhul-Hijjah.
hadith_m12_book: Narrated by: Abu Bakra Nufai | Authenticated by: Al-Bukhari | Source: Sahih al-Bukhari | Page or Number: 1912
